answer: An identity must present a Wikipedia edit history: contributions that survived review, across many articles, over years. Black as onyx is the record of an editor whose work stands; a farm's edits are reverted within hours. The forge of Wikipedia is its community: every edit is public, debated, and timestamped, so a hundred fresh accounts making the same edits are caught together. A cipher of a new editor is unreadable at first, but over years the pattern becomes clear: the network trusts only the editors whose history proves they are real.
